:::{#exm-cross-product-sum-outer}
#### The Gram matrix and a cross-product as sums of outer products

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
$\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$
from @exm-cross-product-matrix,
so $\vecf{r}_1 = (1, 0)$, $\vecf{r}_2 = (1, 1)$, $\vecf{r}_3 = (0, 1)$.
With $\matr{B} = \matr{A}$, the [Gram matrix](#def-gram-matrix) is the [sum](algebra.qmd#def-summation) of the [outer products](linear-algebra-inner-products.qmd#def-outer-product) of the rows with themselves:

$$
\ba
\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{A}}
&= \vecf{r}_1\,\tp{\vecf{r}_1} + \vecf{r}_2\,\tp{\vecf{r}_2} + \vecf{r}_3\,\tp{\vecf{r}_3}
&& \text{(@thm-cross-product-sum-outer)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-outer-product)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}.
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

This is the Gram matrix of @exm-gram-matrix.
For the column $\matr{B}$, the rows are the [numbers](number-systems.qmd#def-real-numbers) $s_i = 1, 2, 3$, so

$$
\ba
\tprod{\matr{A}}{\matr{B}}
&= 1 \vecf{r}_1 + 2 \vecf{r}_2 + 3 \vecf{r}_3
&& \text{(@thm-cross-product-sum-outer)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(scalar multiples)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix},
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

the same as in @exm-cross-product-matrix.

:::
